citations.title: Admission standards
citations.requirement: Admit and retain only people whose needs the home may lawfully meet. Lists 13 people who may not be accepted or retained, including those needing continual medical or nursing care, chronically bedfast, chronic unmanaged incontinence, or danger to self or others. Requires a medical evaluation (DSS-3122) within 30 days before admission and at least every 12 months, and a written administrator interview. Applicants receive the admission agreement, rights statement, facility rules and Ombudsman/legal-services sheet at or before the interview, and may review the latest DOH inspection report. Requires persistent efforts at alternative placement when a resident can no longer be retained.

citations.title: Resident protections
citations.requirement: (a) Resident rights statement: posted, given at admission, reviewed annually, with 19 minimum rights. (b) Resident organizations. (c) Written grievance system with posting of the procedure. (d) Admission agreement content, including SSI/HR personal-allowance offer and refunds. (f) Termination: 30 days' written notice on a DOH form, list of free legal and advocacy services, copy to the regional office within 5 days, and a court proceeding if the resident objects.

citations.title: Resident funds and valuables
citations.requirement: Governs the operator's handling of resident funds and valuables. Section number and title confirmed from the Part 487 table of contents. Body text NOT fetched; confirm detail before citing a subdivision.

citations.title: Resident services
citations.requirement: (a) Minimum services: room, board, housekeeping, supervision, personal care, case management, activities. (d) Supervision duties, evacuations, missing-resident steps, emergency and illness response, death, suicide attempt and felony reporting, and the Incident Report triggers. (e) Personal care, including a ban on physical restraints and monthly weights. (f) Medication management: self-administration, staff assistance limits, secure storage, no injectables by staff (except licensed staff), no dose changes without physician authorization.

citations.title: Food service
citations.requirement: Food service standards for adult homes. Section number and title confirmed from the Part 487 table of contents. Body text NOT fetched; food staffing hours come from §487.9(j).

citations.title: Personnel
citations.requirement: Orientation and in-service training with documentation (a)(3)-(5). Staffing schedules kept 12 months (a)(6). Personnel records (a)(7). Annual physician/PA/RN statement plus TB assessment (a)(8). Staff must speak, read and write English (a)(13). First-aid-trained person on duty at all times (a)(15). Notify the regional office within 3 business days of key vacancies (a)(16). Justice Center staff exclusion list check (a)(7), (a)(17). Administrator approval, hours and qualifications (c). Resident volunteers and employees (b). Supervision census table, personal care 3.75 hrs, housekeeping 1.0 hr and food service 2.0 hrs per resident per week ((f)-(j), per the fact-checked research).

citations.title: Records and reports
citations.requirement: Resident and facility records (c)-(d). Quality assurance plan updated at least every two years, with a quality improvement committee meeting at least every six months (d)(5)(ix). Annual financial statement DSS-2963, quarterly statistical report, quarterly resident roster (e). Mandated forms (f). Postings (g). Retention (h): 3 years after death or discharge for individual records, 7 years for program, business and renewal records.

citations.title: Environmental standards
citations.requirement: Per the fact-checked research: sprinklers throughout buildings of 25+ beds, bedroom minimums of 100 sq ft single and 160 sq ft double, 1 toilet per 6 and 1 bath per 10 residents, and a call system.

citations.title: Disaster and emergency planning
citations.requirement: DOH-approved written disaster and emergency plan. Monthly staff fire drills at varied times, with full and partial evacuation. Quarterly drills with residents, and one total evacuation every 12 months. Annual observation of a resident drill by fire authorities, a certified service agency or DOH. Drill records. Notify DOH by the next business day of a work stoppage, fire, loss of a fire system, no hot water or loss of essential services. HPN account with 24/7 contacts, kept current monthly.

citations.title: Reporting of reportable incidents
citations.requirement: Facilities subject to the Justice Center, and their mandated reporters, report a reportable incident to the Justice Center immediately on reasonable cause. The facility must start an investigation. These duties are in addition to the other reporting duties in Part 487.

citations.title: Enriched housing program personnel
citations.requirement: For enriched housing programs: program coordinator hours, case manager 0.5 hr per resident per week, and 6 hrs per resident per week of combined personal care, housekeeping and food staff (per the fact-checked research).

citations.title: Enriched housing resident services (cross-reference only)
citations.requirement: Cross-referenced in 10 NYCRR 1001.10(l)(1) for medication (488.7(d)) and 1001.10(i) for case management (488.7(e)) when the ALR is certified as an enriched housing program. Text NOT fetched.

citations.title: ALP resident services and services in the capitated rate
citations.requirement: Defines ALP resident services and the services covered by the Medicaid capitated rate (per the fact-checked research).

citations.title: ALP personnel
citations.requirement: Designated individual, qualified case manager, and minimum staffing at the §487.9(f)(6) levels (per the fact-checked research).

citations.title: Applications for ALR licensure and EALR/SNALR certification
citations.requirement: Must also hold an adult home or enriched housing certificate. 60-day response rule. ALR approval lapses if the residence is not licensed and operating within 1 year. Licensure fee rules (per the fact-checked research).

citations.title: ALR admission/individualized service plan provisions (cross-reference only)
citations.requirement: Cross-referenced in 1001.10(c) and (j)(1) as the source of the individualized service plan (ISP) requirement (cited there as 1001.7(h) and (k)). Title and text NOT fetched. Confirm the subdivision before citing.

citations.title: ALR residency agreement provisions (cross-reference only)
citations.requirement: Cross-referenced in 1001.10(c)-(d) (1001.8(f)) as the source of the signed residency agreement that must list services and additional charges. Text NOT fetched.

citations.title: Resident services (ALR)
citations.requirement: Minimum ALR services: housing, 24-hour on-site monitoring, daily food service, case management, ISP, and personal care and/or home care. Residents may use outside providers and choose their own health care providers. Case management duties include evaluation before admission and at least every 12 months using the DOH personal data and resident evaluation form. Health services come from an Article 36 home care agency unless EALR/SNALR-approved. Hospice permitted without EALR when conditions are met. Medication policies must meet 18 NYCRR 487.7(f)/488.7(d). Medication assistance record and PRN rules. EALR and SNALR service rules, including the 24-hour skilled nursing retention exception.

citations.title: Personnel (ALR)
citations.requirement: Case manager on site at least 20 hrs/week under 25 beds, scaled up to 40 hrs/week at 45+ beds. Resident aides: 40 hrs initial training, 12 hrs annual in-service, and an annual performance assessment with direct observation. Orientation topics and written job descriptions. Bloodborne pathogen exposure program and post-exposure procedure. EALR/SNALR: RN 8 hrs/day 5 days/week, LPN 8 hrs/day the other 2 days, RN on call 24/7, with a waiver option at 40 or fewer beds. Immunization and TB records for EALR/SNALR direct-care staff. Advanced home health aide rules.

citations.title: ALR personnel records (cross-reference only)
citations.requirement: Cross-referenced in 1001.10(i)(8) and 1001.11(c)(2)(iii), (e) for resident and personnel record content. Text NOT fetched.

citations.title: ALR structural and environmental standards
citations.requirement: Additional structural standards for ALRs. SNALR beds must be in a fixed area (per the fact-checked research).

citations.title: Assisted living definitions (Art. 46-B)
citations.requirement: ALR means 5 or more residents with 24-hour on-site monitoring. ALP is excluded from the definition.

citations.title: Enhanced assisted living certification and aging in place
citations.requirement: EALR certification and aging-in-place rules, including the physician's report.

citations.title: General requirements; fees; quality reporting and price posting
citations.requirement: ALR biennial fee. ALRs must post starting monthly rate, rent range, approved agreement and fee summary on the website and in the facility, and report annual quality measures to DOH. Operating an ALR without approval is a class A misdemeanor (§4656(5)).

citations.title: Establishment of adult care facilities; eligible operators; ownership changes
citations.requirement: Eligible operator structures. DOH approval of LLC articles before filing. Transfer of 10% or more of interests needs prior DOH approval, and smaller transfers need 90 days' notice (§461-b(9)). Operating without approval is a class A misdemeanor (§461-b(2)(d)).

citations.title: Assisted living program (Medicaid)
citations.requirement: ALP eligibility. Requires a LHCSA or CHHA under identical ownership and PHHPC approval. Case-by-case public need review for new beds from April 1, 2025.

citations.title: ALP capitated rate methodology
citations.requirement: ALP capitated rates equal 50% of low-intensity nursing home prices by wage-equalization region.

citations.title: Operating certificates
citations.requirement: Certificate term up to 4 years, non-transferable. Facility may not use a designation not on the certificate (§485.5(f)). 120-day written notice and DOH-approved plan before closure (§485.5(k)).

citations.title: Application for operating certificate
citations.requirement: Part I and Part II approval. Part II must include the disaster plan, admission and residency agreements, personnel policies and service plans. Final inspection requirements.

citations.title: Renewal of operating certificates
citations.requirement: Apply for renewal 45 to 90 days before expiration.

citations.title: Inspections/surveys of adult care facilities
citations.requirement: Cited in the fact-checked research as the basis for recertification surveys every 12 or 18 months. Correct cited violations within 30 days (research checklist).

citations.title: Posting of complaint line and resident rights materials
citations.requirement: Cited in the fact-checked research for posting the DOH ACF complaint line (1-866-893-6772) and resident rights materials. Do Not Refer List consequences.

citations.title: Termination of admission/residency agreements (cross-reference only)
citations.requirement: Cited in 10 NYCRR 1001.10(m)(5) as the statutory proceeding for terminating the residency agreement of a resident who needs 24-hour skilled nursing care. Text NOT fetched.

citations.title: Justice Center mandated reporting, staff exclusion list, code of conduct (cross-references only)
citations.requirement: Cited inside 18 NYCRR 487.9(a)(3)(vii)-(viii), (a)(7) and (a)(17) and 487.10(i) for reportable incidents, mandated reporters, the staff exclusion list (SSL 495), State Central Register consultation (SSL 424-a) and the Justice Center code of conduct (Exec. Law 554). Statutory text NOT fetched.

citations.title: HIV/bloodborne pathogen exposure definitions (cross-reference only)
citations.requirement: Cited in 10 NYCRR 1001.11(h) as defining significant risk exposure for the ALR exposure prevention program. Text NOT fetched.

citations.title: Confidential HIV-related information (cross-reference only)
citations.requirement: Cited in 18 NYCRR 487.10(d)(3)-(4) for confidentiality of HIV-related information on residents, employees, volunteers, applicants and prospective residents. Text NOT fetched.

citations.title: Paid sick leave
citations.requirement: 40 hours of paid sick leave for 5-99 employees, 56 hours for 100+ (per the fact-checked research).

citations.title: Minimum wage
citations.requirement: From 1/1/2026: $17.00/hr in NYC, Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester; $16.00/hr elsewhere. General rates stay the same on 1/1/2027. Home care aide minimum for LHCSA aides is $19.65/$18.65 in 2026 and $20.00/$19.00 on 1/1/2027 (per the fact-checked research).

citations.title: Home health aide training (cross-reference only)
citations.requirement: Cited in 10 NYCRR 1001.11(n), (p), (r)(2) for home health aide training in EALR/SNALR. Text NOT fetched.

citations.requirement: 10 NYCRR 1001.10(h)(2) requires all food purchasing, storage, preparation and service to comply with Part 14 of Title 10 and local health codes. Part 14 text NOT fetched.

citations.title: Controlled substances and professional misconduct provisions on medication (cross-reference only)
citations.requirement: 10 NYCRR 1001.10(l)(2) requires ALR medication policies to comply with these sections and with 18 NYCRR 487.7(f)/488.7(d). Text NOT fetched.

citations.title: Medicaid provider compliance programs
citations.requirement: Not in the fact-checked research and NOT fetched. Included from general knowledge for ALP (Medicaid) billing integrity. Confirm applicability thresholds before citing.

citations.title: Managed long term care (ALP exclusion)
citations.requirement: People enrolled in the assisted living program are not eligible for MLTC (per the fact-checked research).

policies.title: Operator, Governing Body and Administrator Responsibilities
state_specifics: The operator must employ an administrator, or act as one if qualified. The administrator is directly accountable to the operator for compliance (18 NYCRR 487.9(c)(1)).

The administrator must be capable of and responsible for supervision, regulatory compliance, staff recruitment, resident services, admission/transfer/discharge, protecting rights, a grievance system, and investigating and reporting allegations of reportable incidents to DOH (487.9(c)(8)).
Eligible operator types are set by SSL 461-b(1)(a).
In an ALR, the operator designates an individual responsible for operating the residence in compliance (10 NYCRR 1001.11(a)).

policies.title: Administrator Qualifications, DOH Approval, Hours and Continuing Education
state_specifics: No one may be designated administrator without prior written DOH approval (487.9(c)(2)). DOH may withdraw approval and impose civil penalties (487.9(c)(3)).

Minimum on-duty day hours: 40 hrs/week at 25+ beds, 20 hrs/week at 24 beds or fewer (487.9(c)(4)-(5)). At 24 beds or fewer the administrator may also serve as case manager and activities director and may perform other duties for up to 10 of the 20 hours (487.9(c)(6)).

Age and character: at least 21, with 3 recent letters of recommendation (487.9(c)(9)(i)-(ii)). Education and experience by size: 24 beds or fewer, HS + 3 yrs (1 supervisory), or associate + 2 yrs, or bachelor's + 1 supervisory yr. 25-90 beds: HS + 4 yrs (2 supervisory), associate + 3 yrs, bachelor's + 2 yrs. 90+ beds: HS + 5 yrs, associate + 3 yrs (2 supervisory), bachelor's + 2 supervisory yrs (487.9(c)(9)(iii)-(v)).

Continuing education: 60 clock hours per 2 years with prior DOH approval (487.9(c)(15)). Waived for a licensed nursing home administrator (487.9(c)(16)). 30 hours per 2 years with a post-baccalaureate degree (487.9(c)(17)). Include 15 hours on mental disability care if there are significant numbers of mentally disabled residents (487.9(c)(15)(iv)).
Notify the regional office within 3 business days of a vacancy in administrator, case manager, activities director, dietary consultant or health consultant (487.9(a)(16)).

policies.title: Licensure Stack (Operating Certificate, ALR/EALR/SNALR, ALP), Posting and Regulatory Compliance
state_specifics: An ALR must also hold an adult home or enriched housing operating certificate. EALR and SNALR are add-ons. ALP is a separate approval under SSL 461-l.
Operating certificates last up to 4 years and are non-transferable. Apply for renewal 45-90 days before expiration (18 NYCRR 485.5, 485.7).
ALR fee: $500 + $50 per resident above 400% FPL (max $5,000) biennially. EALR or SNALR adds $2,000, both $3,000. ALR approval lapses if not operating within 1 year (PHL 4656; 10 NYCRR 1001.5).
Do not use any designation (e.g., 'assisted living') not on the certificate or license (485.5(f)).

Post: operating certificate, latest inspection report with follow-ups, rights statement, weekly menus, monthly activities schedule, evacuation procedures, no-gratuity notice, personal-allowance access times, and grievance procedures (487.10(g)). Post the DOH ACF complaint line 1-866-893-6772.
Surveys occur every 12 or 18 months. Correct cited violations within 30 days (per research checklist).
ALR price posting and annual quality measures (PHL 4656(7)). Post starting monthly rate, rent range, approved agreement and fee summary on the website and in the facility.

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
state_specifics: Records documenting QA plans must be updated at least bi-annually (487.10(d)(5)(ix)).
Keep program records, business records and application/renewal records for 7 years (487.10(h)(3)).
ALR staff must be oriented to ALR/EALR/SNALR policies and procedures, and each position needs a current written job description (10 NYCRR 1001.11(f)-(g)).
Policies on DOH-prescribed topics (e.g., TB follow-up, 487.9(a)(8)(ii)(a); HPN coverage reviewed at least annually, 487.12(k)) need documented annual review dates.

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Quality Improvement Committee
state_specifics: Develop and maintain a QA plan for each area of operation. It must include performance standards (including infection control), measurement of adherence, identification of failures, and corrective action (487.10(d)(5)(ix)).

Quality improvement committee must meet at least every 6 months. It includes the administrator or operator, the resident council president or other resident representative, and frontline staff from each operational area.
The committee may not examine personally identifiable resident incidents.
ALRs report annual quality measures to DOH and post them (PHL 4656(7)).

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
state_specifics: Applies in full to ALP (Medicaid) billing. ALP is paid fee-for-service at DOH provider-specific per diems by RUG-II category. ALP enrollees are not in MLTC (PHL 4403-f). Rate questions go to ALP-Rates@health.ny.gov.
Private-pay-only ALRs: apply the anti-gratuity rules in 487.5(a)(3)(xvi) and (d)(6)(ix).
Confirm the SSL 363-d/18 NYCRR Part 521 compliance-program thresholds with counsel (not verified here).

policies.title: Ownership Change, Operating Certificate Renewal and Facility Closure
state_specifics: Transfer of 10% or more of interests in the operating entity needs prior DOH approval. Smaller transfers need 90 days' notice (SSL 461-b(9)).
Closure requires written notice to the regional office at least 120 days ahead and a DOH-approved closure plan (18 NYCRR 485.5(k)).
Records required by DOH stay in the facility on change of operator (487.10(h)(1)).
Renewal application 45-90 days before expiration (485.7).

policies.title: Resident Rights and Responsibilities
state_specifics: Adopt the DOH statement of rights and responsibilities. Post it in a conspicuous public area, give it to each resident at admission, and review it annually (487.5(a)(1)-(2)).

Cover the 19 rights in 487.5(a)(3), including private communication, mail unopened, privacy in room, choice of roommate and private room if affordable, decorating, no gratuities, own version of incident events, control of schedule with access to food of preference at any time, and the right to object to termination.
Residents may not be restrained or locked in a room (487.5(a)(3)(xii)). Residents are not required to work for the facility (487.5(a)(3)(xv)).
Residents may not be confined to room or bed (except short-term illness), no in-room tray service except short-term illness, and commodes only with limits (487.7(e)(4)-(6)).

policies.title: Grievances, Recommendations and Resident Council
state_specifics: Written grievance system must include: designated staff, confidential submission option, timely evaluation and resolution, and informing residents of the outcome (487.5(c)(2)). Post the procedure and staff names (487.5(c)(3)).
If the facility is subject to the Justice Center, conspicuously display its hotline number where residents, staff, volunteers and contractors can see it (487.5(c)(3)).
Residents may grieve to the DOH or other officials without reprisal (487.5(a)(3)(iv)). The DOH ACF complaint line is 1-866-893-6772.
Resident council: encourage and assist it. Residents chair it. Appoint a staff advisor. Give a written response to issues raised (487.5(b)).

policies.title: Long-Term Care Ombudsman and Legal/Advocacy Access
state_specifics: At or before the admission interview, give the Ombudsman Program fact sheet (if provided to the operator) and the DOH list of legal and advocacy agencies (487.4(q)(4)).
Every termination notice must include a list of free legal services and advocacy agencies, including the Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program, with names, addresses and telephone numbers (487.5(f)(5)).
Residents may join with others to work for improvements and may communicate privately with anyone of their choosing (487.5(a)(3)(iii), (v)).

policies.title: Admission/Residency Agreement, Fees, Deposits and Refunds
state_specifics: Use the DOH model admission/residency agreement and EALR, SNALR and ALP addenda. Agreements are pre-approved in Part II (per research).

Required content (487.5(d)(6)): effective date, payment due dates, required services and basic rate, a schedule of optional services with charges only at resident option, and the allowed rate-adjustment grounds. Those grounds are resident written approval, an emergency, physician order, or 30 days' written notice of increased operating cost.

The agreement must also state: any money or property given to the operator; the SSI/HR personal-allowance account offer; bed-reservation charge (not above the basic rate); termination terms and grounds; a prorated refund of advance payments; final accounting on discharge; and annual medical evaluation.
Waivers of required provisions are void (487.5(d)(4)). No life-care contracts (487.5(e)).
ALR: services listed in the signed residency agreement must match the ISP, and additional services and charges must be specified (10 NYCRR 1001.10(c)-(d)). Post prices per PHL 4656(7).
SSI Congregate Care Level 3 for 2026 is $1,688/month ($994 federal + $694 state), with a $262 personal needs allowance.

policies.title: Resident Funds, Personal Allowance Accounts and Personal Property
state_specifics: Offer each SSI or HR recipient (or representative payee) the chance to place personal funds in a facility-maintained account and record acceptance or rejection. A signatory who declines must comply with the personal allowance requirement (487.5(d)(6)(xi)-(xii)).
Use DOH forms: Statement of Offering (DSS-2853), Personal Allowance Summary (DSS-2855), Personal Allowance Ledger, and Inventory of Resident Property (DSS-3027) (487.10(f)).
Post the schedule of times residents may access personal allowance accounts (487.10(g)(8)).
Keep a payment account, personal fund account and current inventory of property held (487.10(c)(4)(i)).
On discharge or transfer, give a final written statement and immediately return all money and property (487.5(d)(6)(xviii)).
See also §487.6 (Resident funds and valuables). Its body text was not fetched.

policies.title: Advance Directives and Health Care Decision-Making
state_specifics: Medical evaluation (DSS-3122) and admission interview must capture representative information (487.4(g)-(h)).
The residents' right to manage their own affairs and choose medical providers is in 487.5(a)(3)(vi).

No specific adult-home advance-directive section was verified. Policy should reference NY Health Care Proxy Law, MOLST and Family Health Care Decisions Act practice as general state law. Confirm statutory cites with counsel before publishing.

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality, HIV-Related Information and HIPAA
state_specifics: Residents have the right to confidential treatment of personal, social, financial and health records (487.5(a)(3)(x)).
Records must be kept so as to assure resident privacy yet remain accessible to staff for routine and emergency services (487.10(c)(3)).
Confidential HIV-related information on residents, employees, volunteers, applicants and prospective residents must be kept per 18 NYCRR 485.11(g)(9)-(15) (487.10(d)(3)-(4)).
Records required by the operator may not be posted or made available to the public (487.10(d)(6)).
Resident version of incident events is on every Incident Report unless the resident objects (487.7(d)(13)).

policies.title: Nondiscrimination, Mobility Impairment Accommodation and Language Access
federal: ADA Title III, 42 USC 12181 et seq.
state_specifics: Do not exclude a person because of mobility impairment. Make reasonable accommodations consistent with federal, state and local law (487.4(b)).

If the applicant or resident is sight- or hearing-impaired or cannot comprehend English or printed matter, arrange the interview and the explanation of agreement, rights and facility information in a comprehensible manner (487.4(s)).
Direct-contact staff must speak, read and write English and speak the predominant language of residents (487.9(a)(13)).
Residents' civil and religious liberties may not be infringed (487.5(a)(3)(i)-(ii)). Residents may choose roommates (487.5(a)(3)(viii)).

policies.title: Pre-Admission Screening, Medical and Mental Health Evaluation, and Admission Criteria
state_specifics: Do not admit before determining the program can meet the person's physical, psychological and social needs. The determination is based on a medical evaluation, an administrator (or designee) interview with the resident and representative, and a mental health evaluation if there is a known or suggested chronic mental disability (487.4(f)-(g)).

Medical evaluation (DSS-3122 or approved substitute) is signed by a physician, PA or NP. It must be based on a physical exam within 30 days before admission, and repeated at least every 12 months or on a change in condition (487.4(h), (k)).
Interview content and a written summary with date and attendees are required (487.4(j)).
Hospital, SNF or psychiatric admissions need a referral-source statement of significant conditions (487.4(o)).
Do not exceed the certified capacity (487.4(d)).
Applicants receive the agreement, rights statement, rules, and an opportunity to review the latest DOH inspection report (487.4(q)-(r)).
Transitional adult homes must obtain a DOH pre-admission screening for serious mental illness (487.4(e)). Apply this only if the facility is so designated.
ALR case manager must meet the prospective resident before admission and explain basic ALR, EALR and SNALR levels of service (10 NYCRR 1001.10(i)(3)-(4)).

policies.title: Resident Assessment and Annual Reassessment
state_specifics: Case manager identifies and evaluates the resident's needs, interests and strengths before admission and at least every 12 months using the DOH personal data and resident evaluation form (10 NYCRR 1001.10(i)(1)).
Medical (and, where required, mental health) evaluations are repeated at least every 12 months and on a change in condition (487.4(k)(2)).
Personal Data Sheet DSS-2949 is mandated (487.10(f)(1)).
Assist residents in obtaining required evaluations (487.4(l)).

policies.title: Case Management and Individualized Service Plan
state_specifics: Case management is a required service (487.7(a)). ALR case manager oversees and coordinates a written individualized service plan (ISP) for each resident (10 NYCRR 1001.10(i)(2)).
Case manager hours (ALR): under 25 beds at least 20 hrs/week on site. 25-44 beds, 20 hrs + 1 hr per bed over 24. 45+ beds, at least 40 hrs on site (1001.11(c)(1)).

Case manager duties also include information and referral, coordination with provider(s) chosen by the resident, and a formal mechanism to flag abrupt or progressive changes in behavior or appearance (1001.10(i)(5)-(7)).
DOH approval of the case manager is required for adult homes. The administrator may be designated case manager under 50 beds if qualified (per research).
ISP must specify necessary health care services, including those from a licensed home care agency (1001.10(k)(1)). See §1001.7 for ISP content (cross-reference, not fetched).

policies.title: Retention Limits and Conditions the Facility Cannot Serve
state_specifics: Never accept or retain a person who: needs continual medical or nursing care; has a serious and persistent mental disability warranting a Mental Hygiene Law facility; needs services that cannot be provided safely by local providers; is a danger to self or others; repeatedly impairs the well-being of others or the orderly operation of the facility; has an unstable condition needing continual skilled observation; refuses or cannot comply with prescribed treatment (including medications) where a physician finds life-threatening danger; is chronically bedfast; has chronic unmanaged urinary or bowel incontinence; has a dangerous communicable disease; depends on medical equipment unless all six conditions in 487.4(c)(11) are met; has aggressive or destructive alcohol or drug use; or is under 18 (487.4(c)).

If a resident cannot be retained, document persistent efforts: 5 applications, telephone follow-up every 2 weeks, a new application within 5 working days of a rejection, and a written report to the regional office every 90 days if not placed (487.4(m)).

EALR (aging in place) may retain residents with a physician's report. EALR and SNALR residents needing 24-hour skilled nursing must be discharged unless the four conditions in 10 NYCRR 1001.10(m)(5) are met.
Hospice retention conditions are in 1001.10(k)(4).

policies.title: Involuntary Discharge, Transfer and Relocation Notice
state_specifics: Give at least 30 days' written notice on a DOH-prescribed form to the resident, next of kin (if known) and any designated responsible party (487.5(f)(3)).

Notice must state the reason, date, and right to object. If the resident objects, they may stay while the operator commences a court proceeding (487.5(f)(4)). Prior court approval is required (487.5(d)(6)(xvi)(c)).
Attach the free legal and advocacy services list. File a copy of the notice with the regional office within 5 days of service (487.5(f)(5)-(6)).

Allowed involuntary-discharge reasons are limited by 487.5(f)(14) (e.g., continual medical or nursing care the facility is not licensed to provide). The remaining list was not fully captured here. Review the full subdivision.

Shorter-notice transfer is allowed for conditions requiring continual skilled care and for imminent risk of death or serious harm. Seek police assistance where possible. Readmit when the basis no longer exists. If transferred without notice, hand-deliver the termination notice at the new location (487.5(f)(7)-(11)).
Residents may object to a termination (487.5(a)(3)(xix)).

policies.title: Medication Management, Storage and Disposal
state_specifics: Medications are kept in secure storage (locked, cannot be removed or entered at will) at all times, except when a resident must carry them for frequent or emergency use (487.7(f)(11)(i)-(ii)).
To retain controlled substance prescriptions the operator must first obtain a class 3a Institutional Dispenser, Limited license from DOH (487.7(f)(11)(iii)).

Store external-use drugs separately from internal and injectable drugs. Do not store drugs in a food refrigerator unless in a separate locked compartment. Do not pour medications between containers (except for temporary absences). Only a physician or pharmacist may change label directions (487.7(f)(11)(iv)-(vii)).
ALRs must have medication policies and procedures that meet 487.7(f)/488.7(d), 10 NYCRR 80.5 and 80.6, and 8 NYCRR 29.7(a)(21)(ii)(b), and follow DOH guidance (1001.10(l)(1)-(2)).

Maintain a medication assistance record for each resident, covering diagnoses, all prescription and OTC medications, indication, special directions, allergies and a photo or electronic identifier (1001.10(l)(3)).
The disposal procedure text in 487.7(f) was cut off in the fetched copy. Confirm it against the full section before finalizing.

policies.title: Assistance with Self-Administration of Medication and Staff Authorization Limits
state_specifics: A resident may self-administer if the physician attests in writing to capability and the resident keeps the operator informed of all medications (487.7(f)(1)-(2)).
For residents needing help, staff provide the proper dose at the designated time and observe and record that it is taken. The person assisting must remove the dose or prepare it (487.7(f)(5)-(6)).

Staff may not administer injectables, except a licensed professional for injectables that providers customarily train a patient or family to give. Insulin syringes may be prefilled only by a nurse (487.7(f)(6)-(7)).

Notify the prescriber (and the primary physician if different) if a resident refuses or cannot take medications (487.7(f)(8)). Never change dose or schedule without prior written physician authorization. In an emergency, a phone order needs written confirmation within 7 days (487.7(f)(9)).
If another physician prescribes or discontinues a drug, notify the primary physician within 1 business day and document it (487.7(f)(10)).

PRN rules (ALR): the order must state the behaviors or symptoms that warrant the drug. Without a physician statement that the resident can identify the need, assistance with PRN (including OTC) requires observation or consultation with licensed nursing or medical staff and documentation. PRN use for persons with dementia is limited to cases where the physician finds no alternative (1001.10(l)(4)-(7)).
EALR advanced home health aides: must be on the home care worker registry, have 18 hrs annual in-service, and be directly supervised by an RN, with an RN visit at least every 2 weeks (1001.11(r)).

policies.title: Nursing Services, Home Care Agency Arrangements and Delegation (EALR/SNALR Nursing Coverage)
state_specifics: A basic ALR arranges needed nursing, home health aide, therapies, social work, nutrition and supplies through an Article 36 home care agency. A home care agency may not provide the basic adult home or EHP services (e.g., personal care) unless it is under contract to do so and those services are in the basic rate (1001.10(k)(2)-(3)).
Residents may use providers the operator has no arrangement with, and may choose their own health care providers (1001.10(e)-(f)).

EALR/SNALR: RN on duty on site 8 hrs/day, 5 days/week, and an LPN 8 hrs/day the other 2 days. RN on call 24/7 if not on site. Added coverage if the medical evaluation or ISP requires it (1001.11(j)). A 40-bed-or-fewer operator may request a written waiver. It takes effect only on DOH written approval and the operator must disclose it to residents (1001.11(k)-(l)).
When an RN is not on site, provide enough home health aides trained in first aid and medication assistance (1001.11(n)). HHAs also need 12 hrs annual in-service (1001.11(p)).
Before an RN assigns advanced tasks to an advanced HHA, the RN must complete a nursing assessment and medication review. Written patient-specific instructions are required (1001.11(r)).

policies.title: Change of Condition, Physician Notification and Hospital Transfer
state_specifics: If a resident cannot or will not eat regular meals for 2 consecutive days, immediately notify the personal physician, act on instructions and note the call in the record (487.7(d)(5)).

On illness or injury: protect the resident, obtain emergency help, and transfer if necessary. Notify the personal physician (or qualified alternate) and the representative or next of kin (487.7(d)(6)).

On transfer, send the approved transfer form (or the medical evaluation and personal data sheet) and any requested information. For emergency transfers, phone the information and send written information within 72 hours. Note the event in the record (487.7(d)(6)(iii)).
Dangerous behavior: arrange professional evaluation, transfer if necessary, and notify the representative or next of kin (487.7(d)(7)).
Maintain a system so incident and change-of-condition information reaches all shifts (487.7(e)(9)). Take and record weights monthly (487.7(e)(2)(vii)).
Do not admit or accept return from a hospital or SNF without a referral statement (487.4(o)).

policies.title: Dementia and Special Needs Assisted Living (SNALR) Memory Care
state_specifics: Dementia-specific services require SNALR certification and an approved special needs plan (10 NYCRR 1001.10(n); PHL 4655). SNALR beds must be in a fixed area (1001.13; 1001.5(c)(2) per research).

SNALR must operate a comprehensive and coordinated program to regularly observe and assess service needs, and set up community linkages specific to the special-needs population (1001.10(n)(2), (n)(4)).

SNALR supervision: maintain knowledge of the general whereabouts of each resident. If a resident is absent with whereabouts unknown, begin immediate efforts to locate (1001.10(n)(5)). Text beyond this point was not captured.
SNALR nursing coverage rules in 1001.11(j)-(k) apply. PRN prescription drugs for persons with dementia are limited (1001.10(l)(7)).
Doors and egress: residents may not be locked in a room (487.5(a)(3)(xii)). Any secured-unit design must be cleared with DOH Part II/architecture review.

policies.title: Falls Prevention
state_specifics: Supervision duties include monitoring for abrupt or progressive changes in behavior or appearance, and monitoring the emergency call system (487.7(d)(1)(iii), (vi)).
A resident who is assaulted or injured, or who has an accident (on or off grounds) requiring medical attention, triggers an Incident Report DSS-3123 (487.7(d)(11)(ii), (vii)).
ISP changes follow identification of change in function (10 NYCRR 1001.10(g)(2)(ii)).
Call system in bedrooms, toilets and baths (487.11 per research).
The rules verified do not prescribe a fall-risk tool or specific interventions. The policy should set facility-defined procedures consistent with these duties.

policies.title: Skin Integrity and Pressure Injury Prevention
state_specifics: Residents with unstable conditions needing continual skilled observation, or who are chronically bedfast, may not be retained (487.4(c)(6), (8)). Wounds beyond the facility's scope require referral to a home care agency (1001.10(k)(2)).
Personal care includes bathing, toileting, ordinary movement from bed to chair and monthly weights (487.7(e)(2)).
Changes in condition must be reported to all shifts and the physician (487.7(d)(6), (e)(9)).
No skin-specific section was verified. The policy should rely on the personal care, supervision and nursing-referral duties above.

policies.title: Hospice and Home Care Agency Coordination
state_specifics: Hospice is permitted in an ALR without EALR certification if the ALR, the resident's physician and the hospice agree the resident can be safely cared for, responsibilities are written into the ISP, and the operator agrees to retain the resident and coordinate care (10 NYCRR 1001.10(k)(4)).

Home care services in the residence must be provided by an Article 36 agency (1001.10(k)(2)). The operator remains responsible for adult home or EHP basic services even if a contracted home care agency fails (1001.10(k)(3)).
Case manager coordinates with outside providers chosen by the resident (1001.10(e), (i)(6)).

policies.title: Death of a Resident
state_specifics: Immediately notify next of kin or representative (if known) and the appropriate local authorities (487.7(d)(8)(i)-(ii)).
Immediately report the death by telephone to the DOH regional office. The Incident Report must be received within 24 hours (487.7(d)(8)(iii)).
If the resident ever received services from a mental hygiene service provider, send a Justice Center report on its form, received within 24 hours (487.7(d)(8)(iv)).
An Incident Report is required whenever a resident dies (487.7(d)(11)(v)). The administrator or case manager investigates incidents involving death (487.7(d)(1)(x)).
Return money and property to the representative with a final account (487.5(d)(6)(xviii)). Keep resident records for 3 years after death (487.10(h)(2)).

policies.title: Medicaid Assisted Living Program (ALP) Eligibility, Services and Staffing
state_specifics: Applies only if the facility holds ALP approval under SSL 461-l (requires a LHCSA/CHHA under identical ownership and PHHPC approval). Mark this policy N/A for private-pay-only operations.

ALP staffing: at least the 487.9(f)(6) supervision levels, a designated program individual, a qualified case manager (RN, MSW, or degree plus experience), and home-care-trained personal care staff (494.6). Nursing and therapies are inside the capitated service package (494.5).

ALP residents are excluded from MLTC (PHL 4403-f). Rates are provider-specific per diems by RUG-II category, set at 50% of low-intensity nursing home prices by region (PHL 3614(6)). 1/1/2025 statewide medians run from $65.04 (PA) to $118.60 (RB) per day.
LHCSA aides paid at the home care aide minimum: $19.65 downstate and $18.65 elsewhere in 2026, rising to $20.00/$19.00 on 1/1/2027.
New ALP beds approved case by case on public need from April 1, 2025. Existing ALPs in good standing may add up to 9 beds under expedited review (research).

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting (Justice Center / DOH)
state_specifics: First determine with DOH whether the facility is a 'facility' under SSL 488(4) subject to the Justice Center. 487.14 and 487.7(d)(14) apply only if so.

If subject: mandated reporters report any reportable incident immediately on reasonable cause. The Justice Center must receive the report within 24 hours of discovery, including names and contact details of all persons with knowledge (487.14; 487.7(d)(14)).

Start an investigation when an alleged reportable incident occurs. The Justice Center and/or DOH may also investigate (487.14(d)). The administrator must investigate and report to DOH allegations that would constitute a reportable incident (487.9(c)(8)(x)).

Suspected felony crime against or by a resident: call the DOH regional office immediately, send the Incident Report within 24 hours, notify law enforcement within 24 hours, and send a Justice Center report within 24 hours if the resident ever received mental hygiene services (487.7(d)(10)).
A complaint or evidence of resident abuse requires an Incident Report (487.7(d)(11)(iv)).
Residents are to be free from physical, mental and emotional abuse and may not be required to give gratuities (487.5(a)(3)(xi), (xvi)).

Staff training: identification of reportable incidents, reporting procedures, mandated reporter duties, and annual Justice Center code of conduct acknowledgment (487.9(a)(3)(vii)-(viii)). Post the Justice Center hotline number (487.5(c)(3)). Confirm the current number with the Justice Center before posting.

policies.title: Incident and Accident Reporting
state_specifics: Prepare Incident Report DSS-3123 when: whereabouts unknown more than 24 hours; assault or injury by or to a resident; suicide attempt or death; abuse complaint or evidence; behavior that impairs others' well-being or operations; an accident on or off grounds requiring medical attention; or a suspected felony (487.7(d)(11)).

Place a copy in the resident's record. Keep a chronological log of all Incident Reports with resident and incident type. Submit copies to the DOH regional office. Contact the Justice Center where required (487.7(d)(12)).
Include the resident's version of events unless they object (487.7(d)(13)).
24-hour DOH timeframes: death, attempted suicide, and suspected felony (487.7(d)(8)-(10)).
Notify DOH by the next business day of a fire, work stoppage, loss of a fire system, no hot water, or interrupted essential services (487.12(j)).
Incident reports about an employee belong in the personnel file (487.9(a)(7)(i)).

policies.title: Elopement and Missing Resident
state_specifics: Supervision includes knowing each resident's general whereabouts and recording a daily census on the DOH form (DSS-2900) (487.7(d)(1)(i)-(ii)).

If a resident's whereabouts are unknown, start efforts to find the resident. If absence exceeds 24 hours: immediately notify next of kin or representative; immediately notify law enforcement; notify the regional office on the first available working day; and send the Incident Report to the regional office within 5 working days (487.7(d)(4)).

Residents are not to be locked in (487.5(a)(3)(xii)). Residents may engage in community life as they prefer, with recognition of safety (487.5(a)(3)(xiv)). SNALR has its own immediate-search duties (1001.10(n)(5)).

policies.title: Restraints and Restrictive Practices
state_specifics: Physical restraints (any apparatus preventing free movement of arms or legs or immobilizing a resident who cannot remove it) shall not be used (487.7(e)(7)).
Residents must be free from coercion and restraint, and may not be restrained in any way or locked in a room (487.5(a)(3)(xi)(c), (xii)).
Residents may not be confined to their room or bed except for short-term illness. Sick bay use is limited (487.7(e)(4), (e)(8)).
Chemical restraint: staff may not change medication dosage or schedule without physician authorization (487.7(f)(9)). PRN psychotropics for persons with dementia are restricted (1001.10(l)(7)).

policies.title: Emergency Preparedness and Disaster Plan (including HPN Communications)
state_specifics: Written plan approved by DOH (submitted in Part II). Plan must include: staff responsibilities, full and partial evacuation, preliminary relocation plans, coordination with community resources and local emergency planners, and plans for maintaining service with reduced personnel (487.12(a)-(b)).
Train every new and current employee and volunteer on the overall plan and their own role. Review performance after each drill (487.12(c)).
Post evacuation procedures on every floor and in each wing. Keep emergency contact numbers and procedures available to supervisory staff (487.12(d)-(e)).

HPN accounts: designate HPN coordinators and users, maintain a 24/7 emergency contact in the HPN directory, update the directory as changes occur (at minimum monthly), and review the HPN coverage policy annually (487.12(k)).
Notify DOH by the next business day of any circumstance requiring implementation of the plan (487.12(j)).
At least one staff person per shift is designated to run evacuation or the disaster plan (487.7(d)(3)). Federal CMS emergency preparedness CoPs do not apply to this program.

policies.title: Fire Safety, Evacuation and Drills
state_specifics: Monthly fire drills for staff and volunteers at varied times (day and night), with full and partial evacuation and simulated fire conditions (487.12(f)).
At least one fire drill each calendar quarter must include residents. At least one drill every 12 months must be a total evacuation (487.12(g)).
Arrange at least annually for local fire authorities, a certified service agency or DOH to observe a resident drill (487.12(h)).
Record date, time, description, number of residents, and signatures of participating staff and volunteers (487.12(i)). Keep drill records (487.10(d)(5)(iv)).
Sprinklers throughout buildings of 25+ beds, with at least one fire protection system connected to the local fire department (487.11(b)(4), (6) per research).
All employees must be trained in rapid evacuation (487.7(d)(2)).

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control, Bloodborne Pathogens and Exposure Management
state_specifics: ALR: implement and enforce a program preventing exposure to significant-risk body substances. It must include protective barriers, safe handling of sharps and contaminated equipment, training at hire and annually, PPE, and compliance monitoring (10 NYCRR 1001.11(h)).

ALR: exposure-management policy with reporting to a designated person, evaluation of the exposure, source-individual assessment and counseling, medical follow-up of the exposed individual, and confidentiality. HIV status disclosure requires express written consent or a court order (1001.11(i)).
Residents with communicable diseases that endanger others may not be retained (487.4(c)(10)). Staff with communicable disease may not work (487.9(a)(11)).
A sick bay or isolation area is permitted within certified capacity (487.7(e)(8)).
The QA plan must include infection control performance standards (487.10(d)(5)(ix)).
EALR/SNALR direct-care staff: rubella and measles immunization records, unless exempt (1001.11(q)).

policies.title: Smoking, Visitors and Pets
state_specifics: Facility regulations on resident activities, office and visiting hours must be given to applicants at or before the admission interview (487.4(q)(3)).
Residents may have private communications with anyone of their choice and may not be denied community life (487.5(a)(3)(iii), (xiv)).
Residents may decorate their rooms in compliance with fire and safety codes (487.5(a)(3)(ix)).
No verified provision addresses smoking or pets. Policy content is facility-set. Check NY Clean Indoor Air Act and local fire code.

policies.title: Resident Supervision, Daily Census and Call System Monitoring
state_specifics: Supervision services: maintain knowledge of general whereabouts, record the daily census on the DOH form, monitor for changes in behavior or appearance, guide basic ADLs, surveil grounds and activities, monitor emergency call systems, handle emergencies, conduct evacuations and drills, implement the disaster plan, and investigate incidents (487.7(d)(1)).
Staff on duty and on site 24 hours a day: 1 for census 1-40, 2 for 41-80, 3 for 81-150, 4 for 151-200, plus 1 per additional 60 (487.9(f)(6) per research).
At least one first-aid-qualified person on duty and on site at all times (487.9(a)(15)).
ALR: 24-hour on-site monitoring with the ability to respond to urgent needs and to identify abrupt or progressive changes (1001.10(g); PHL 4651).

policies.title: Food Service and Therapeutic Diets
state_specifics: Food service staffing: at least 2.0 hrs per resident per week and never under 35 hrs/week (487.9(j)(1) per research). A food service manager is required. A qualified dietitian or dietetic technician supervises under a written agreement stating duties and time (487.9(j)(3)-(4) per research).

ALR food purchasing, storage, preparation and service must follow 10 NYCRR Part 14 and local health codes. Food must respect health conditions, allergies, intolerances, religious and ethnic mandates, and taste preferences (1001.10(h)).

Records must be readily available to food service staff to plan prescribed diets, allergies and preferences (487.10(c)(4)(iii)). Keep menus and food purchase records (487.10(d)(5)(v)). Post weekly menus (487.10(g)(4)).

Residents have access to reasonably available foods of preference at any time (487.5(a)(3)(xviii)). Interviews must confirm the program can meet cultural, religious or prescribed dietary needs (487.4(j)(2)(i)).
No in-room tray service except for short-term illness (487.7(e)(6)). See §487.8 (not fetched).

policies.title: Activities and Social Programming
state_specifics: Activities is a required resident service (487.7(a)). Personal care includes helping residents participate in the activities program (487.7(e)(3)).
Post the monthly activities schedule (487.10(g)(5)). Keep activity schedules as program records (487.10(d)(5)(iv)).

At 24 beds or fewer the administrator may be activities director. At 50+ beds, qualified activities staff are required (research). Report an activities director vacancy to the regional office within 3 business days (487.9(a)(16)).
Interviews must confirm the program meets social needs and fosters family and community ties (487.4(j)(2)(ii)). Residents are not required to participate in facility work (487.5(a)(3)(xv)).

policies.title: Housekeeping, Laundry and Maintenance
state_specifics: Housekeeping staffing: at least 1.0 hr per resident per week (487.9(h) per research). Housekeeping is a required service (487.7(a)).
Keep records of maintenance of the physical plant and environmental standards (487.10(d)(5)(vi)).
Environmental standards in 487.11 include bedroom size, toilet and bath ratios, call system and sprinklers. ALRs also meet 10 NYCRR 1001.13.
Report loss of hot water or essential services to DOH by the next business day (487.12(j)).

policies.title: Transportation
state_specifics: No transportation-specific rule was verified. Residents may engage in community life, including life outside the facility (487.5(a)(3)(xiv)).
Accidents on or off facility grounds that require medical attention require an Incident Report (487.7(d)(11)(vii)).
Charges for transport beyond the basic rate must be listed in the admission agreement's supplemental schedule and be at resident option (487.5(d)(6)(v)-(vi)).
Staff who drive residents must meet applicable NY licensing and insurance law (confirm with counsel).

policies.title: Staffing Levels, Supervision and Key-Position Vacancies
state_specifics: 24/7 on-site staff: 1 for census 1-40, 2 for 41-80, 3 for 81-150, 4 for 151-200, plus 1 per additional 60 (487.9(f)(6) per research).
Minimum weekly hours per resident: personal care 3.75 (day and evening shifts), housekeeping 1.0, food service 2.0 with a 35 hrs/week floor (487.9(g)(2), (h), (j)(1) per research).
Maintain current written staffing schedules and keep past schedules 12 months (487.9(a)(6)). DOH may require added staff above 200 census or with special populations (487.9(a)(2)).
ALR case manager hours (1001.11(c)(1)). EALR/SNALR RN/LPN coverage (1001.11(j)). Enriched housing hours (488.9).

Staff under 18 may not have direct supervision responsibility or work without on-site supervision (487.9(a)(14)). Notify the regional office within 3 business days of vacancies in administrator, case manager, activities director, dietary consultant or health consultant (487.9(a)(16)).

policies.title: Background Checks, Justice Center Staff Exclusion List and State Central Register
state_specifics: Before hiring or engaging anyone with direct resident contact, a facility subject to the Justice Center must verify through the Justice Center that the person is not on its staff exclusion list. If not on it, consult the State Central Register (SSL 424-a). Document the verification in the personnel file (487.9(a)(7)(iii)-(iv), (a)(17)).
A person on the staff exclusion list may not be hired or engaged. A State Central Register listing is a factor in the decision but not a bar (487.9(a)(7)(iv)).

Criminal history record checks for direct-care staff are listed in the research checklist under 487.9(a)(7), (17). The criminal-history text was not located in the fetched portion. Confirm the exact authority before citing.
Administrator needs 3 recent letters of recommendation (487.9(c)(9)(ii)).

policies.title: Hiring, Orientation and Ongoing Training
state_specifics: Initial orientation and in-service for employees and volunteers: population characteristics and needs; resident rights and facility rules; staff duties; the individual's specific duties; emergency procedures; and, if subject to the Justice Center, reportable incidents, reporting procedures and mandated reporter duties (487.9(a)(3)).
Give the Justice Center code of conduct at hire and annually, with signed acknowledgment of receipt and understanding. Also give it to contractors with resident contact (487.9(a)(3)(viii)).
Ongoing in-service training and participation in work-related training (487.9(a)(4)). Document date, time, topic and names of trainers and attendees (487.9(a)(5)).

ALR orientation covers staff duties, service procedures, response to emergencies, evacuation and disaster plan, and personal appearance (1001.11(f)). Each job needs a written job description (1001.11(g)).
Personal care in-service training plan submitted to DOH. New personal care staff complete training within 3 months (487.9(g)(4)-(5) per research).
Bloodborne pathogen training at hire and yearly (1001.11(h)(3)).

policies.title: Resident Aide Training and Competency (ALR)
state_specifics: Resident aides: 40 hours of initial training under the DOH curriculum or approved equivalent (10 NYCRR 1001.11(c)(2)(i)).
12 hours of ongoing in-service annually in topics relevant to responsibilities (1001.11(c)(2)(ii)).
Annual performance assessment of all resident aides including at least one direct observation (1001.11(c)(2)(iv)).
Keep training records in each aide's personnel file (1001.11(c)(2)(iii); see 1001.12, not fetched).
EALR/SNALR home health aides: training per 10 NYCRR 700.2 plus first aid and medication assistance training. 12 hours annual in-service (1001.11(n), (p)).

policies.title: Employee Health Assessment and TB Screening
state_specifics: At hire and at least every 12 months: a statement from a physician (or a PA or RN with special primary-care training under physician oversight) who has physically examined the person, confirming no health impairment that risks residents or impedes duties (487.9(a)(8)(i)).

TB risk assessment, symptom evaluation and TB test (skin test or FDA-approved blood assay) before employment, with annual assessments. Positive findings need clinical follow-up. The operator must have a policy on positive findings, including facilitating and documenting latent TB treatment. Annual assessment includes education, risk assessment and follow-up tests (487.9(a)(8)(ii)(a)).
Any test required by the local board of health (487.9(a)(8)(ii)(b)). Religious-exemption documentation rules are at 487.9(a)(9).

No one with mental illness or substance habituation that endangers self or others or prevents duties may work (487.9(a)(10)). No one with a communicable disease that endangers residents (487.9(a)(11)).
ALR: health status assessed and documented before assuming resident care duties (1001.11(d)). EALR/SNALR direct-care staff also need rubella and measles immunity records (1001.11(q)).

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Each employee record contains verification of required qualifications, medical evaluation, and any incident reports involving the employee. Payment records contain all wages, benefits, reimbursements, bonuses, gifts or payments (487.9(a)(7)(i)-(ii)).
If subject to the Justice Center, include documentation of the staff exclusion list and State Central Register checks (487.9(a)(7)(iii)).
Keep staff records, job descriptions, staffing schedules and payment records (487.10(d)(5)(vii)). Retain program and business records 7 years (487.10(h)(3)).
ALR personnel records follow 10 NYCRR 1001.12 (not fetched), including training records (1001.11(c)(2)(iii), (e)).
Keep HIV-related employee information confidential (487.10(d)(4)).

policies.title: Staff Conduct, Professional Boundaries, Gratuities and Resident Work
state_specifics: No operator, administrator, employee or agent may accept any remuneration or gratuity for services. Post a no-gratuity notice (487.5(d)(6)(ix); 487.10(g)(7)). Residents may not be required to give gratuities (487.5(a)(3)(xvi)).
Justice Center code of conduct given and acknowledged at hire and annually (487.9(a)(3)(viii)).
Resident volunteering: only without coercion or threats, not substituting for required paid staff, and not inconsistent with the resident's needs (487.9(b)(1)).
Resident employment: no coercion, fair compensation, and compliance with labor law. Keep written records of each instance, including name, tasks, rate and hours (487.9(b)(2)-(3)).
Staff must maintain clean, appropriate dress and hygiene and be emotionally, mentally and physically able to perform (487.9(a)(12)).

policies.title: Wages, Paid Sick Leave and Labor Law Compliance
federal: FLSA, 29 USC 201 et seq. (29 CFR 552 only for home care aides in an ALP LHCSA)
state_specifics: 2026 minimum wage: $17.00/hr in NYC, Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester; $16.00/hr elsewhere. Rates stay the same on 1/1/2027.
LHCSA aides (ALP personal care): home care aide minimum of $19.65 (NYC/LI/Westchester) and $18.65 (rest of state) in 2026. $20.00 and $19.00 from 1/1/2027.
Paid sick leave: 40 hours for 5-99 employees, 56 hours for 100+ (Labor Law 196-b).
Payroll records are part of personnel records (487.9(a)(7)(ii)). Register for NY UI. Carry workers' compensation, disability and paid family leave coverage (per research).

policies.title: Resident Records and Retention
state_specifics: Keep complete, accurate and current records for each resident in the facility, available to DOH staff (487.10(c)(1)-(2)).
Financial record: current admission agreement, payment account status, personal fund account, inventory of property held (487.10(c)(4)(i)).
Personal record: personal data, next of kin and emergency contact, medical and mental health evaluations, social evaluation summaries, referral details and correspondence (487.10(c)(4)(ii)).

Mandated forms: DSS-2949 Personal Data Sheet, DSS-2900 Daily Census Record, DSS-3123 Incident Report, DSS-3122 Medical Evaluation, DSS-3027 Inventory of Resident Property, personal allowance forms, and the Mental Health Evaluation (487.10(f)).

Retention: individual resident records 3 years after death or discharge. Program and business records 7 years (487.10(h)(2)-(3)). Also keep a chronological admission and discharge register (487.10(d)(5)(iii)).
ALR resident records per 10 NYCRR 1001.12 (not fetched).

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Annual Financial Statement DSS-2963: due by the 15th day of the sixth calendar month after fiscal year end. An independent accountant's opinion is required at capacity of 10 or more (487.10(e)(1)).

Quarterly statistical information report and a quarterly resident roster to DOH (487.10(e)(2), (e)(5)). Facilities with 80+ beds and 20%+ serious mental illness have additional quarterly and monthly reports (487.10(e)(3)-(4)).

Incident-driven reports: death, attempted suicide and suspected felony (24 hours); missing resident (next working day plus report in 5 working days) (487.7(d)(4), (8)-(10)). Justice Center reports within 24 hours (487.7(d)(14)).
Termination notices to the regional office within 5 days of service (487.5(f)(6)). Persistent-efforts reports every 90 days (487.4(m)(2)(iv)).
Vacancy notice within 3 business days (487.9(a)(16)). Next-business-day notice of emergencies or loss of services (487.12(j)).
ALR: annual quality measures and price reporting (PHL 4656(7)).

policies.title: Posting of Required Documents and Notices
state_specifics: Post: operating certificate; latest inspection report and follow-ups; statement of resident rights; weekly menus; monthly activities schedule; evacuation procedures; notice prohibiting employee gratuities; schedule of times residents may access personal allowance accounts; and procedures for presenting grievances (487.10(g)).
Post the Justice Center hotline number where residents, staff, volunteers and contractors can see it, if subject to the Justice Center (487.5(c)(3)).
Post DOH's ACF complaint line, 1-866-893-6772 (SSL 460-d per research).
Post ALR starting monthly rate, rent range, approved agreement and fee summary, on the website and in the facility (PHL 4656(7)).
Evacuation procedures must be posted on every floor and in each wing (487.12(d)).

forms.name: Medical Evaluation (DSS-3122)
forms.purpose: Physician/PA/NP evaluation within 30 days before admission and at least every 12 months
